        - heading "Understand Motion Analysis" [level=2]
        - paragraph: "Motion analysis uses derivatives of position to study velocity and acceleration. In Motion Analysis, that statement is the exact rule used on the labelled chart and in the three numerical examples. A useful rule is Motion derivatives: v=s'(t), a=v'(t)=s''(t). You can learn Motion Analysis by trying one small example instead of long theory."
        - paragraph: Start with position as a function of time. Differentiate once for velocity. Differentiate again for acceleration. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
        - paragraph: "In real life, car trip: Position, speed, and acceleration are linked. Watch out: Using position value as velocity. Velocity is derivative of position."
